steps.label: Simplify to a tangent
steps.margin_note: First mark. Dividing numerator and denominator by cos11° turns every term into a tangent, and the 1 becomes tan45°, giving tan(45° + 11°) = tan56°.
steps.memory_tip: Divide top and bottom by cos11°, giving tan(45° + 11°) = tan56°.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by cos11° and applying tan(A+B) gives tanθ = tan56°.

steps.why: Dividing by cos11° makes every term a tangent and turns the 1 into tan45°, which is exactly the tan(A + B) form. The quadrant condition comes next; it does not change this simplification.

steps.label: Use the quadrant condition
steps.margin_note: Second mark, and the point of the question. tan is positive in the third quadrant too, and the third-quadrant angle with the same tangent is 180° + 56°.
steps.memory_tip: tan is positive in the THIRD quadrant too, so the answer is 180° + 56° = 236°.
lines: θ is in the third quadrant, and

recall.must_convey: That the third-quadrant condition gives θ = 180° + 56° = 236°, not 56°.
accept: tan repeats every one eighty so the third quadrant angle is one eighty plus fifty six which is two thirty six

the answer is two hundred thirty six degrees

theta is two thirty six degrees

steps.why: tan has period 180°, so two angles in a full turn share any given tangent. The quadrant condition is what picks which one is meant.

insider_note: The simplification gives tan56°, but that is only the reference angle. The third-quadrant condition then adds 180°, so the answer is 236° and not 56°.
